DOID:0050553.definition: A proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome that is characterized by early childhood onset of annular erythematous plaques on the face and extremities with subsequent development of partial lipodystrophy and laboratory evidence of immune dysregulation and that has_material_basis_in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PSMB8 gene on chromosome 6p21. Digenic forms of PRAAS1 can be caused by heterozygous mutation in the PSMB8 gene and heterozygous mutation in either the PSMA3 gene on chromosome 14q23 or in the PSMB4 on chromosome 1q21.

has_subtypes.description: Autosomal dominant form, corresponding to MONDO:0013067 (cataract 34, multiple types; OMIM:612968), caused by heterozygous FOXE3 alleles that extend the protein past its native stop codon. Phenotypes are highly variable and include congenital cataract (cerulean type and early onset nuclear/cortical cataract), Peters anomaly, iris colobomas, and other anterior segment defects. Penetrance is high with variable expressivity, and in the largest reported dominant series eye size was normal in most individuals even though a minority had microphthalmia, aphakia or sclerocornea more typical of recessive disease.

evidence.explanation: Describes the variable phenotypic spectrum of dominant FOXE3 mutations including cataracts and anterior segment anomalies.
evidence.reference_title: Seeing clearly: the dominant and recessive nature of FOXE3 in eye developmental anomalies.
evidence.snippet: the dominant mutations were penetrant, they gave rise to highly variable phenotypes including iris and chorioretinal colobomas, Peters' anomaly, and isolated cataract (cerulean type and early onset adult nuclear and cortical cataract)

evidence.explanation: Identifies a dominant non-stop FOXE3 mutation causing congenital cataract.
evidence.reference_title: Identification of dominant FOXE3 and PAX6 mutations in patients with congenital cataract and aniridia.
evidence.snippet: A novel dominant mutation at the stop codon of FOXE3, c.959G>C (p.X320SerextX72), was identified in a patient with congenital cataract

evidence.explanation: Supports this subtype's composition - cataract with variable anterior segment anomalies in a normal-sized eye - and the overlap with recessive disease that the description records.
evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive phenotypic and functional analysis of dominant and recessive FOXE3 alleles in ocular developmental disorders.
evidence.snippet: In dominant pedigrees, caused by extension variants, normal eye size (96%), cataracts (99%) and variable anterior segment anomalies were seen in most, but some individuals had microphthalmia, aphakia or sclerocornea, more typical of recessive disease.

evidence.explanation: The original dominant FOXE3 family, and the report OMIM indexes as the basis of the cataract 34 / anterior segment dysgenesis 2 designation this subtype is bound to.
evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the human forkhead transcription factor FOXE3 associated with anterior segment ocular dysgenesis and cataracts.
evidence.snippet: An insertion of G in the coding region of the FOXE3 gene that occurred 15 nucleotides upstream of the stop codon was identified in a family with anterior segment ocular dysgenesis and cataracts.

has_subtypes.name: Congenital Cataract

has_subtypes.description: Autosomal recessive form, corresponding to MONDO:0012456 (congenital primary aphakia, also labelled anterior segment dysgenesis 2 or ASGD2; OMIM:610256), caused by biallelic FOXE3 loss-of-function alleles. Characterized by bilateral congenital absence of the lens (aphakia) with secondary aplasia of the anterior segment, sclerocornea, microphthalmia, and in some cases optic disc coloboma. Results from early developmental arrest of the lens placode around the 4th-5th week of embryogenesis.

evidence.explanation: First identification of FOXE3 as the causative gene for congenital primary aphakia in humans.
evidence.reference_title: Homozygous nonsense mutation in the FOXE3 gene as a cause of congenital primary aphakia in humans.
evidence.snippet: Congenital primary aphakia (CPA) is a rare developmental disorder characterized by the absence of lens, the development of which is normally induced during the 4th-5th wk of human embryogenesis

evidence.explanation: Confirms the full recessive phenotype including sclerocornea, aphakia, microphthalmia, and optic disc coloboma.
evidence.reference_title: Homozygous FOXE3 mutations cause non-syndromic, bilateral, total sclerocornea, aphakia, microphthalmia and optic disc coloboma.
evidence.snippet: MRI or ultrasonography confirmed that the patients with sclerocornea were also aphakic, had microphthalmia and some had optic disc coloboma

evidence.explanation: Quantifies the recessive triad of corneal opacity, aphakia and microphthalmia across sixteen families, and records that a minority present with isolated cataract instead.
evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive phenotypic and functional analysis of dominant and recessive FOXE3 alleles in ocular developmental disorders.
evidence.snippet: Most families with recessive alleles, composed of truncating and forkhead-domain missense variants, had severe corneal opacity (90%; sclerocornea in 47%), aphakia (83%) and microphthalmia (80%), but some had milder features including isolated cataract.

has_subtypes.name: Primary Aphakia

mondo_mappings.mapping_justification: This entry covers the FOXE3-related ocular spectrum, including primary aphakia and cataract 34, which ClinGen groups together (CCID:009236). The MONDO target is broader: anterior segment dysgenesis also includes PITX3- and CPAMD8-related disorders. Retain this broader grounding pending a gene-specific MONDO grouping for the combined FOXE3 spectrum.

tracked_issues.title: Proxy MONDO request for FOXE3-related anterior segment dysgenesis

omimps_mappings.mapping_justification: The FOXE3 spectrum overlaps this phenotypic series through congenital primary aphakia (OMIM:610256, anterior segment dysgenesis 2). The January 2026 series also enumerates anterior segment dysgenesis caused by other genes, while this entry includes FOXE3-related cataract 34 (OMIM:612968), which is not enumerated in that series snapshot. Record the overlapping classification scopes without equating the combined FOXE3 spectrum with the series or treating absent enumeration as biological exclusion.
